title: Pairs of organisms collide, bond and orbit, more so with cilia active

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Pairs of organisms collide, bond and orbit, more so with cilia active

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Collective behaviours predicted in simulation were observed in vivo: two organisms often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond and orbit each other for several revolutions before detaching, and this is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Collective Behavior.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For instance, two designs often collide, form a temporary mechanical bond, and orbit about each other for several revolutions before detaching along tangential trajectories (SI Appendix, Fig. S10). This phenomenon is more pronounced when cilia are not inhibited on the organisms

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Results › Collective Behavior.”. Scope: Multiple Xenopus reconfigurable organisms sharing a dish, with and without cilia

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The behavior and treatment contrast admit straightforward video analysis. Existing supplementary records cover examples but may be insufficient for robust frequency estimates and adjustment for locomotion confounds.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track organism pairs and score collision, attachment duration, orbit count, and detachment angle, then compare rates between cilia-active and cilia-inhibited conditions and simulations.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cilia inhibition may alter speed and collision frequency as well as bonding behavior.

Sample sizes and complete encounter-level records may be unavailable.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.92
data adequacy: 0.42
discriminating power: 0.72
data existence: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Contact duration and revolutions are countable, and the deposited simulator covers the in silico collective runs. The cilia comparison and the living orbiting bouts are qualitative and not in that repository. Hydrodynamic sticking remains a competing account of temporary orbits, so current materials test only part of the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In paired trials, score collision rate, duration of mechanical contact, and number of shared revolutions, with cilia intact versus inhibited; the claim holds if orbiting bouts are more frequent when cilia are active.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Orbiting can arise from generic hydrodynamic drafting once two bodies touch.

The cilia contrast is an in vivo observation without a deposited event log.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.5
data existence: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.35
discriminating power: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.7
